cis_text.title: Allowlist Authorized Scripts

ai_guidance.agent: Restrict execution of scripts by agents (e.g., Python code generated by the agent) to only authorized, signed, or sandboxed scripts. Agents capable of generating and executing code (e.g., code interpreters) present a massive risk; allowlisting ensures that they cannot execute arbitrary malicious scripts on the host system.
ai_guidance.mcp: For MCP servers implemented in Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or shell, enforce strict script execution controls by allowing only pre-approved scripts and dependencies. Verify integrity with cryptographic hashing or code signing. Prefer reproducible builds and CI enforcement that blocks unapproved dependency changes before artifacts are produced.

evidence.rationale: Startup scripts not on the allowlist cannot execute, disrupting persistence.
Unauthorized PowerShell scripts fail execution under enforced script allowlisting.
Script allowlisting prevents execution of unauthorized AppleScript files under enforced script validation policies.
Non-authorized batch or shell scripts are blocked.
Unauthorized shell scripts fail execution when enforced through script hash/signature/path validation.
Malicious VB scripts/macros are prevented if not allowlisted.
Unauthorized Python scripts are blocked when interpreter policies enforce script validation.
Script enforcement blocks execution of non-authorized JavaScript files invoked via host interpreters.
Macro scripts blocked if script enforcement applies to macro execution policies.
If script payload execution is enforced regardless of invoking binary, proxy-based script execution is reduced.
PowerShell profile persistence relies on executing a script at interpreter startup. Script allowlisting prevents unauthorized profile scripts from executing.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
